name: Order history: numbered completed orders, quotes and favourite lists for the buyer

dependsOn.why: The orders, quotes and lists belong to the buyer that recipe creates with a password.
Order and quote lines name products the catalogue created.
A line is charged the buyer's price when it is added, and the order stores that total: prices first, or the history carries list prices.

mcpOnly.reason: The numbering, completion and quote reads are Management API (GetNumbers, NumberSave, GetOrderList: search_orders leaves quotes out and is_order_complete answers bare text); no MCP or Management API write creates a favourite list or backdates an order.

hosted.reason: No MCP or Management API write creates a favourite list, sets an order's date or the number counter, or creates an order state without a flow id. Every other step, the reset included, is MCP or Management API.

steps.title: Set the order number series' prefix and postfix

bindings.reason: The ORDER series exists on every install; a site without it is not a Swift commerce site.

steps.trap: NumberSave writes prefix and postFix and keeps the stored counter whatever counter it is sent; the next order takes the series at once, with no flush.

bindings.reason: NumberSave answers ok and keeps the stored counter (sent 5000, read back 1); no MCP tool reaches EcomNumbers, so the counter moves only by placing orders or by a local SQL update.

steps.title: Find the buyer who owns the history

bindings.reason: The buyer, its account and its password are created by the users.accounts recipe; this recipe gives an existing buyer a history.

steps.title: Find the order state each history state is set to

bindings.reason: create_order_state needs the id of the order flow the state belongs to, which the input does not name; build the flow with the order-states reference, then name the state here.

steps.title: Find the user who owns each order: its user, else the buyer

bindings.reason: The owners are created by the users.accounts recipe; this recipe gives existing users a history.

steps.trap: An order of another user than the buyer names it in user; it must be a customer user the customer-centre page shows the order to.

steps.title: Find each product an order line names

bindings.reason: Products are created by the catalogue recipe; a history only names them.

steps.title: Start each order as the buyer's cart, keyed by its reference (the purchase order number)
steps.trap: An order is found again only by its reference: convert_cart_to_order gives it a new id, so no step keeps the cart id. No MCP write sets the order reference (OrderReference), so this recipe keys an order on the purchase order number; a layer copy that keyed it on its reference is that delivery (find.delivered, DELIVERED): never written a second time, and its lines are checked and never added to.

steps.title: Put each line on its order, priced at what the buyer's account pays unless the line states a price
steps.trap: A line added without a price takes the buyer's price at that quantity (the contract, group or tier row), as the cart would.

steps.title: Place each order: convert the cart, which numbers it from the series
steps.trap: convert_cart_to_order takes the next number of the ORDER series; create_orders with orderType Order can collide on the number.

steps.title: Complete each order that is not open, so the buyer's order history lists it
steps.trap: Only search_orders with completedStatus Completed tells a completed order from an open one (completedDate is the only completion member it returns, and is_order_complete answers bare text). The delivery API order list shows completed orders only; complete_order keeps the state, so the state is set after it.

steps.title: Date each new order daysAgo before today

bindings.reason: No MCP tool and no Management API command sets an order's date: create_orders and update_orders carry none and OrderSave stamps now. Out of product it is local SQL keyed on the order id, written last.

steps.title: Find each product a quote line names

bindings.reason: Products are created by the catalogue recipe; a history only names them.

steps.title: Find the user who owns each quote: its user, else the buyer

bindings.reason: The owners are created by the users.accounts recipe; this recipe gives existing users a history.

steps.trap: A quote of another user than the buyer names it in user; it must be a customer user the customer-centre page shows the quote to.

steps.title: Ensure each quote for the buyer in its quote state, keyed by its reference
steps.trap: search_orders leaves quotes out, so a quote is found through the Management API GetOrderList with OrderType Quote. The quote states are the default quote flow's state ids (QuotePending, QuoteSent, QuoteAccepted, QuoteRejected).

steps.title: Put each line on its quote
Ensure each favourite list of the buyer, with its products

bindings.reason: No MCP tool and no Management API command writes a favourite list (EcomCustomerFavoriteLists). The signed-in buyer creates one with POST /dwapi/ecommerce/favorites/lists {name, description, isDefault} and adds products with POST /dwapi/ecommerce/favorites/items/{listId} {productId, quantity, note}; a recipe writes through MCP or the Management API only.

steps.trap: A favourite list is found by name through the delivery API as its owner: no MCP or Management API read lists another user's favourites.

steps.title: Return the history to the seeded state: remove the buyer's orders and carts the input does not name
steps.trap: search_orders lists the buyer's orders and carts and leaves quotes and soft-deleted orders out; force true soft-deletes a cart, an open order and a completed one alike (reversible), and the row leaves the read at once. On a site a layer copy delivered the history to (the orders step reports DELIVERED: the copy stores the input's reference in reference, not in purchaseOrderNumber), the reset removes only rows with a purchase order number, the mark create_orders writes on every order this recipe makes; the copy's orders and its seeded cart carry none, and neither does a storefront rehearsal order, so all of them are DELIVERED and left alone (measured on a first build on a layer-delivered site, where the reset would otherwise have deleted three delivered orders and the seeded cart). Remove a rehearsal order there by hand.

steps.title: Return the quotes to the seeded state: remove the buyer's quotes the input does not name
steps.trap: GetOrderList honours UserId and ignores CustomerId and the like, so the scope check on customerAccessUserId is what keeps another buyer's quote out; a quote soft-deleted with delete_order leaves GetOrderList at once.

probes.title: The signed-in buyer's order history lists each completed or rejected order
The signed-in buyer sees each quote
The signed-in buyer sees each favourite list
Each order placed after the numbering step carries the series prefix

provenOn.evidence: orders.completed-orders.1-verify.json (numbering WOULD-UPDATE, orders, lines and quote WOULD-CREATE, the favourite list a delivery-API fixture UNCHANGED), 2-apply.json (series prefix set, three orders and a quote created, lined, placed and stated; the order dates OPEN as planned) and 2b-apply.json after the completion read was rebuilt on search_orders (30 of 30), 3-verify and 4-apply-again (30 of 30, nothing written), 6-hosted-verify without SQL (30 of 30); 5-mcponly.json is 23 of 30 (numbering and quotes need the Management API, the favourite list and the probes the delivery API); 7-verify-reset.json reports the reset OPEN as planned. The signed-in buyer was served both completed orders, the quote and the favourite list; the orders took RCPC-4 to RCPC-6 from the series after the step, a blank series having numbered ORDER1; a rehearsal order force-deleted with delete_order left the buyer's list at once.

The reset as two prune steps, scoped to the buyer the history names: r1-verify listed four stale carts WOULD-DELETE and r2-apply soft-deleted them (35 of 35); two orders the buyer then placed through the delivery API cart (additems, payment, shipping, createOrder) were listed WOULD-DELETE and nothing else by r3-verify (31 of 33), removed by r4-apply (33 of 33) and absent from r5-verify (32 of 32): the buyer's delivery API order list was back to the two seeded completed orders and search_orders to the three seeded orders, untouched. A rehearsal quote was listed by r6-verify and removed by r7-apply (32 of 32). r8-mcponly is 24 of 32: the order and cart reset runs MCP-only, the quote reset needs the Management API read.

the whole-build recipe set on a fresh fictional input after the add-in was rolled 0.6.3-BETA -> 0.6.6-BETA (Update-HostAddIn): 1-verify (all eleven recipes WOULD-CREATE), 2-apply, 3-verify (11 of 11 recipes), 4-apply-again (nothing written, no debt owed), 5-verify after a brand restore (11 of 11); the same input then verified 11 of 11 on the add-in rolled back to 0.6.3. 6-mcponly is an MCP-only apply on a second fresh input. This recipe: 22 of 22 (the order dates OPEN in the apply as planned); MCP-only 17 of 22, numbering and quotes need the Management API.

the same delivered-copy site: the six orders and the quote the copy keyed on their reference DELIVERED through find.delivered (one order owned by its user, not the buyer), their 13 lines checked UNCHANGED, placed, completed and state DELIVERED, no WOULD-CREATE; -Apply wrote only the order number prefix the copy does not carry (orders 6, quotes 1, lines 13 before and after). From empty [mcp 0.6.6-BETA]: 25 of 25, apply again nothing written.

the proof site, a fictional buyer with an order the copy keyed on its reference, a seeded cart with no marks and a stale cart of the recipe's own shape (a purchase order number the input no longer names): verify listed only the stale cart WOULD-DELETE and the other two DELIVERED, -Apply deleted only it, and a second verify passed 6 of 6 with nothing to delete.

traps: No debt: the delivery API listed a completed order, a quote and a list on the next request, and the next converted order took the new prefix.
A line added without a price is charged the buyer's price at its quantity, the lowest of contract, group and tier rows; the order stores line and order totals.
create_orders leaves the order's customer number empty; the buyer's delivery API list finds it by user id (RetrieveMode useUserId), a customer-number list does not.
A blank site numbers orders ORDER1, ORDER2: the ORDER series prefix is ORDER and its counter 0.
An order's id changes when its cart is converted; its reference (purchase order number) is the only key that survives.
The delivery API lists a buyer's completed orders only, and quotes only through ecommerce/orders/search with Type quote.

The reset removes by soft delete (delete_order force true): reversible, and gone at once from search_orders, GetOrderList and the buyer's delivery API lists. It is scoped to the buyer's user id; an order of another user, or a read that ignored its filter, refuses the reset with nothing deleted.

A buyer's delivery API checkout (carts/create with languageId, countryCode and currencyCode, then carts/additems, PATCH payment and shipping, createOrder) completes the order at once and numbers it from the series, with no purchase order number, so the reset finds it unnamed; the cart becomes the order and leaves no cart behind.
